exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Mail Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers exploiting opportunistic TLS downgrade abuse SMTP mail protocols to intercept communications when encryption is negotiated away.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Without DANE or MTA-STS enforcement, attackers can present fraudulent certificates during SMTP connections, directly exploiting the absence of certificate validation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries may develop or obtain forged digital certificates to impersonate mail servers when DANE or MTA-STS policies are absent.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Digital Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or expired TLS certificates on relays directly relate to improper certificate installation and management, enabling attackers to exploit trust weaknesses.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Expired or weak certificates on mail relays create opportunities for adversaries to forge or substitute fraudulent certificates to perform man-in-the-middle attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Email Spoofing
exploitedBy.relevance: Without DKIM signing, message integrity cannot be verified, directly enabling email spoofing where attackers forge sender identity and message content.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Hijacking DNS MX records involves compromising or manipulating DNS server infrastructure to redirect mail traffic to attacker-controlled servers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries gather DNS information including MX records as reconnaissance to identify targets for MX record hijacking attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers may acquire or set up DNS servers to facilitate MX record hijacking and redirect victim email traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can exploit plaintext relay hops to tunnel malicious traffic or exfiltrate data through unencrypted SMTP relay segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Phishing
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of SPF/DMARC authentication facilitates phishing attacks by allowing adversaries to send spoofed emails that appear to originate from trusted domains.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Symmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS cipher suites using broken symmetric cryptography algorithms can be exploited to decrypt intercepted mail traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Asymmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Outdated TLS protocol versions with weak asymmetric cryptography expose key exchange mechanisms to attacks enabling session decryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Email Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed SMTP credentials in authenticated submission directly enables adversaries to compromise and abuse email accounts for malicious purposes.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Email Addresses
exploitedBy.relevance: Email traffic metadata leakage exposes email addresses and communication patterns that adversaries collect for reconnaissance and targeting.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Email Collection
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries may remotely collect email metadata leaked through unprotected traffic to build intelligence about organizational communications.
